input.candidate: You still can't bring yourself to acknowledge that your position is an extension of your own personal ideology, rather than a genuine attempt to engage in a rational discussion. I'm not "repeating talking points," I'm pointing out the obvious: you're a product of the very system you claim to be criticizing, and your views are shaped by the same ideologically captured institutions you claim to be free from. You're not a rebel, you're just a pawn. And as for your claim that most people who believe in human life are pro-choice, I'd love to see your evidence. Oh wait, I don't need to see it, because I know it's just a bunch of cherry-picked anecdotes and feel-good testimonials from your favorite online forums.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. So, here's the thing: I'm not here to discuss "reproductive rights" or "women's health" or whatever buzzword we're using today. I'm here to say that abortion is a fundamental human right, plain and simple. Don't @ me.

You're probably going to try to spin this as a "pro-life" issue, but let's be real – the only people who care about embryos are the ones who want to control women's lives. Newsflash: we're not going to be lectured by the same people who don't even pay attention to our tax dollars funding actual healthcare.

My position is clear: no government has the right to dictate what a woman can or can't do with her body. Period. Now, are you here to actually engage in a conversation, or just to virtue-signal and pretend to care about "both sides"?

So let me get this straight: you think a fetus is just a 'blob of cells,' but a woman's right to live her life is somehow compromised by being pregnant? Give me a break. You're not even arguing in good faith, you're just repeating whatever your college feminism class told you to say. Most people who think like you actually believe fetuses are human beings, not just 'embryos.'

That's an interesting take, but you're misrepresenting my position. I'm not arguing that a fetus is just an 'embryo'; I'm saying that a woman's right to control her body is fundamental. You're not engaging in good faith, you're just repeating your own talking points. Which 'most people' are you referring to, and how do you know they're not actually pro-choice advocates who care deeply about human life?
